'''Dmitri Dmitriyevich Ryutov''' (Russian: Дми́трий Дми́триевич Рю́тов; born March 6, 1940, in [[Moscow]]) is a Russian theoretical plasma [[physicist]].

== Early life and career ==
Ryutov graduated from the [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]] in 1962 and from the [[Kurchatov Institute]] in 1965, where he received his doctorate in plasma theory in 1966. From 1968 to 1997, he was at the [[Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics]] in [[Novosibirsk]], where he expanded the fusion research program from 1979 and was promoted from deputy director to chief scientist in 1994. He was also a professor of plasma physics at the [[Novosibirsk State University]]. From 1994, he was a senior visiting scientist at the [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]] (LLNL), where he became a Distinguished Member of the Technical Staff in 2012. Ryutov retired from LLNL in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.llnl.gov/news/lab-scientist-earns-award-plasma-physics|title=Lab scientist earns award for plasma physics {{!}} Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory|website=www.llnl.gov|access-date=2020-02-22}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Ryutov has been a corresponding member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] since 1976 and a full member since 1992. He became a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1998 and the [[Institute of Physics]] in 2004. He became an Edward Teller Fellow of the LLNL in 2007 and received the [[Distinguished Career Award]] from Fusion Power Associates in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.llnl.gov/news/fusion-interests-powers-ryutov%E2%80%99s-llnl-career|title=Fusion of interests powers Ryutov's LLNL career {{!}} Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory|website=www.llnl.gov|access-date=2020-02-22}}</ref>

In 2017, he received the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] for ''"many outstanding contributions to the theoretical plasma physics of low and high energy density plasmas, open and closed magnetic configurations, and laboratory and astrophysical systems".''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Ryutov&first_nm=Dmitri&year=2017|title=2017 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=2020-02-22}}</ref> 

In 2020, Ryutov, with 10 other researchers from different institutions, jointly received the [[John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research]] for the generation of [[Weibel instability|Weibel-mediated]] collisionless [[Shock wave|shocks]] in laboratory plasma experiments.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2020 John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research Recipient|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Ryutov&first_nm=Dmitri&year=2020|access-date=2020-07-24|website=American Physical Society|language=en}}</ref> He was part of a team that studied and observed Weibel-mediated collisionless shocks at the [[National Ignition Facility]] of LLNL.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fiuza|first1=Frederico|last2=Spitkovsky|first2=Anatoly|last3=Ryutov|first3=Dmitri|last4=Ross|first4=Steven|last5=Huntington|first5=Channing|last6=Mori|first6=Warren|last7=Silva|first7=Luis|last8=Park|first8=Hye-Sook|author8-link=Hye-Sook Park|last9=Remington|first9=Bruce|date=2013|title=Driving Weibel-mediated collisionless shocks with NIF|journal=APS Division of Plasma Physics Meeting Abstracts|language=en|volume=2013|pages=UO5.007|bibcode=2013APS..DPPUO5007F}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Park|first1=H.-S.|last2=Huntington|first2=C.
